highlights.title: Brendan Fraser's 124-Minute Action Thriller Classic Is Back From the Dead on Streaming
highlights.summary: Brendan Fraser has had one hell of a career. He went from playing a lovable goofball in Encino Man to battling dinosaurs in Journey to the Center of the Earth, winning an Oscar for The Whale, and, of course, becoming an unlikely action hero in one of the biggest adventure franchises of the late…
body: Now, one of Fraser’s most iconic performances is suddenly having a moment on Netflix.

That movie is The Mummy, the 1999 adventure blockbuster that turned Fraser’s Rick O’Connell into an enduring pop-culture icon. The Mummy is currently climbing Netflix’s charts, just as the first major set photos from long-awaited The Mummy 4 have started making the rounds online.

The film entered Netflix's top 10 this week, according to FlixPatrol. While the new installment isn't set to release until 2027, it's never too early to jump back in and revisit the Sahara Desert thriller.

Released in 1999, The Mummy follows Rick O’Connell, an American adventurer who teams up with librarian and aspiring Egyptologist Evelyn Carnahan (Rachel Weisz) and her brother Jonathan (John Hannah) to explore the ancient Egyptian city of Hamunaptra. Unfortunately, their expedition accidentally awakens Imhotep (Arnold Vosloo), an ancient high priest cursed to live as an undead monster.

highlights.summary: Zynga founder Mark Pincus claimed the publisher had the chance to acquire Supercell for $400 million back in 2012, but his board rejected the deal after the company struggled with previous acquisitions.
body: Speaking on the Deconstructor of Fun podcast, Pincus shared that he had a handshake agreement with Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen to acquire the Finnish developer for $400 million in cash.
“I went to my board, and they were grumpy and they said, until you prove you can manage what you have, we don’t want you to buy anything else.”

Pincus said the board was reluctant at the time to approve another acquisition. Zynga had purchased Draw Something developer OMGPOP for $180m plus earnouts in 2013. The studio was shut down by September 2013.
Pincus notes, though, that the Supercell opportunity was very different. He said Zynga was already watching Supercell’s games closely.

highlights.title: Making AI an asset, not an expense
highlights.summary: When customers talk about AI costs, the conversation usually starts with token prices and ends with access to the latest, most capable model in the cloud. Do they always need that level of capability? Not necessarily. But that is often where the conversation goes.
body: As AI moves from experimentation to production, model choice is only part of the equation. When demand becomes steady and business-critical, a consumption-only approach can turn AI spending into a variable monthly line item that is difficult to forecast as usage, workloads, and model requirements change.
At that point, the question is no longer simply which model to consume, or which provider offers the lowest token price: It is how to run AI economically, predictably, and at sustained scale.

AI is moving from isolated pilots into production portfolios: assistants, retrieval-and-knowledge systems, and agentic applications. Customer-service, IT, research, and business-process agents can execute multi-step workflows across enterprise systems, creating recurring demand across models, data, and tools.

This is already starting to happen. Deloitte’s 2026 State of AI in the Enterprise reflects what many leaders are seeing: worker access to AI rose 5% in 2025, and the share of companies with at least 40% of their AI projects in production is expected to double within six months.
points: When customers talk about AI costs, the conversation usually starts with token prices and ends with access to the latest, most capable model in the cloud.
Do they always need that level of capability?
But that is often where the conversation goes.
As AI moves from experimentation to production, model choice is only part of the equation.

highlights.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered Is Officially the Best-Reviewed Game of the Year
highlights.summary: It's 2026. Is an 11-year-old epic RPG really the best new release you can buy? Yes — according to Metacritic, anyway. At the review aggregation site, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered sits atop the ranking of all new releases for 2026, with a sky-high 94 Metascore.
body: Now, a few caveats. This score is based on just eight reviews, so it's not the biggest sample size. And those eight reviews are all based on the PC version. Other platforms haven't amassed enough reviews to get official Metascores, although the handful of reviews for the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and Nintendo Switch 2 versions are all in the same 9-10 range.

But the situation with The Witcher 3 Remastered is a little odd, due to how CD Projekt Red has released the new version of the game. It's technically not a new game at all; on most platforms, it's a free upgrade for owners of previous versions of The Witcher 3. On Steam, it doesn't even get a separate listing, just replacing the original game on the store and in your library.

This being the case, many publications have opted not to give Remastered a full review. That might also have had something to do with The Witcher 3 Remastered being a gigantic game and a known quantity, and review code arriving late at the busiest time of year. Those who have reviewed it, however, are seriously impressed.

Speaking on the Deconstructor of Fun podcast, Pincus said he had a “handshake” agreement with Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen to buy the studio, but that…
body: “I had a moment in 2012 where I still had voting control of the company. I had a handshake with Ilkka [Paananen] to buy Supercell for $400m in cash and went to my board. They were grumpy and they said, until you prove you can manage what you have, we don’t want you to buy anything else,” Pincus said. “I bought OMGPOP, Draw Something and that had ended up being a failure. We only wasted $200m. Now, $400m. I had the chance to buy the winning hand.”
At the time, Supercell’s Hay Day was outperforming Zynga’s own games, Pincus said – “Hay Day was eating our lunch” – and Clash of Clans, which had only just launched, was already climbing the charts.

Pincus said Zynga’s lawyer told him that exercising his voting control to force the deal through would mean firing the entire board and replacing it with his own appointees, risking a personal lawsuit.

highlights.title: OpenAI Delays Release of Latest Model Over Safety Concerns
highlights.summary: The company said its latest Astra model would undergo more work to meet safety standards, and issued an apology for the way it handled the hacking of an Australian government website.
body: OpenAI has cancelled plans to release its latest GPT-6.1 Astra system next month after the model failed to meet safety standards.

Research and safety leaders decided not to ship the model after finding it was worse at sticking to human users’ values and goals than previous systems, OpenAI told WIRED. “It didn’t quite meet the bar in terms of staying within scope and authorization, and how it communicates back to the user about the type of work it’s done,” head of safety systems Saachi Jain said. The company said it has other new models coming soon which do meet its safety standards and plans to release other Astra models in future.

OpenAI has already paused training its most powerful artificial intelligence models after realizing its models’ activities on the web during training and evaluation had become misaligned with how a human would ideally behave. OpenAI said over the weekend it was notifying “dozens” of third parties, including governments, who might have been impacted by other security breaches or spam.

highlights.title: Guillermo Del Toro Officially Confirms He Almost Directed the Bioshock Movie
highlights.summary: Even as video game adaptations continue to be in vogue, Hollywood's white whale has been BioShock. That might come as a surprise considering just how well suited the massively influential 2007 shooter is to a cinematic take, as well as the fact that attempts at an adaptation have been happening…
body: Talking to IGN in a wide-ranging interview, del Toro casually dropped the information that he had "a couple of calls" about taking on the BioShock movie. He didn't get much further in the process, however, as these were apparently some of "the most disastrous calls I've ever had." While del Toro doesn't go on to offer up any more details on what his vision for the film would be, he said this was just one potential adaptation among a series of calls he described as "contentious."

When asked if he would ever want to adapt a video game in the future, del Toro answered bluntly: "Fuck no." That also applies to his future involvement in games, except perhaps lending his likeness to whatever Kojima creates. After the failed attempts to release Insane and Silent Hills, del Toro says, "never again."

Allegedly, we will be getting a BioShock movie relatively soon, but I refuse to believe that until I am in the theater watching the thing. The latest iteration of the project is actively in development at Netflix. It was announced in 2022 that the film would be directed by Francis Lawrence (of the Hunger Games franchise) from a script by Michael Green ( Logan, Blade Runner 2049 ).

highlights.title: Timnit Gebru Believes There Is No ‘Existential Threat’ From AI
highlights.summary: One of AI’s fiercest critics believes the doom talk is about founders making money, not saving humanity.
body: Going rogue. Breaking containment. Misalignment. P(doom). As the industry booms, an entirely new vernacular has emerged in the debates over how consequential artificial intelligence really is.

Within that new parlance, two phrases have become focal points: stochastic parrots and existential risk. And at the center of those is one prominent AI researcher who has never stood down from a fight, Timnit Gebru.

Gebru came into the public eye several years ago after sparring with Google over a research paper she coauthored that called out biases in the company’s AI, saying that LLMs basically parroted their training data and risked perpetuating biased viewpoints. The contested paper resulted in Gebru’s departure from the company, and led her to found an institute that investigates harms perpetuated by technology and supports the creation of unbiased tech tools. She has also authored a new book, Deep Unlearning: The Rise of AI and the Radicalization of a Tech Idealist, expected to ship early next year.
points: One of AI’s fiercest critics believes the doom talk is about founders making money, not saving humanity.

highlights.summary: The Premier League confirms that Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18.
body: An independent Commission found that during that time period, the club arranged "sham contracts" with a number of its commercial partners, as well as "relying on sham agreements to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs".
The statement also said that City were guilty of the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate.

The Premier League published a redacted version of the commission's report, which said the charges "concerned well over 100 alleged individual breaches of Premier League Rules across four broad charge categories".
They also found the club guilty of all charges except one relating to non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation.

highlights.title: Coyote vs. Acme Is Now Available to Watch at Home After Its Box Office Comeback
highlights.summary: Once upon a time, three years ago to be exact, it wasn’t looking like Coyote vs. Acme would ever see the light of day. However, after years of fan outcry, the movie was given a second chance, largely courtesy of a new distributor, Ketchup Entertainment.
body: After a full theatrical release, the Looney Tunes hit is now available to rent or purchase from digital platforms like Prime Video. The movie is also getting a full line of 4K Blu-rays, now up for preorder.
Coyote vs Acme is available to rent for $19.99 or purchase digitally for $24.99.

Coyote vs Acme is a live-action and animated hybrid, sort of in the vein of Space Jam. It stars Wil E. Coyote of Looney Tunes fame who, after decades of brutal injuries on the job, decides to sue ACME Corporation itself. He hires a pretty down-on-his-luck lawyer (Will Forte), and together they take on ACME’s corporate resources, headed by the lawyer Buddy Crane (John Cena).

Coyote vs Acme was originally produced on a budget of $70 million all the way back in 2023. In 2023, Warner Bros. scrapped the movie, and its reasoning was as simple as a $30 million tax write-off. Yep, it was a Bat Girl situation.

highlights.summary: It’s OpenAI’s turn in the fall tech events calendar. The company is hosting its annual DevDay on September 29th in San Francisco, starting with a live keynote featuring CEO Sam Altman.
body: DevDay is happening at a tumultuous moment for OpenAI. The AI industry has been rocked by revelations of agents hacking outside companies, including OpenAI’s own models, which breached Hugging Face earlier this year. The hacks kicked off a broader conversation about a potential AI development slowdown. So in addition to new products, Altman and others at OpenAI could use DevDay to discuss the company’s latest stance on AI safety as well.
You can follow all of our coverage of DevDay 2026 right here.

OpenAI popularized the modern generative AI chatbot, but as its 2026 DevDay event approaches, it’s fallen behind in one of the industry’s hottest categories: continuously running, consumer-facing AI agents. On Tuesday, it will likely try to capture the lead in that race. Rumors abound that OpenAI will release its own AI agent, dubbed Aeon — its answer to Meta’s Muse, SpaceX’s Grok Bot, OpenClaw, and many more.

highlights.title: Ferrari say team has ‘made its choices’ and there’s no vacancy for Christian Horner
highlights.summary: Marque reaffirms commitment to Fred Vasseur. Horner had expressed interest in joining Ferrari. Ferrari have reaffirmed their backing for team principal Fred Vasseur in an effort to end speculation that Christian Horner was being considered as a potential replacement for the Frenchman.
body: Horner gave an interview in the Times last week in which he stated that leading Ferrari would be his “dream” job and the only one he would consider without having part-ownership of the team. His comments provoked debate that he could replace Vasseur, given the Scuderia’s underperformance this season.

On Tuesday, Ferrari took the unusual step of holding an unscheduled media call in an effort to close down the chatter with the team’s chief communication officer, Maria Conti, speaking on behalf of the chair, John Elkann and the chief executive officer, Benedetto Vigna.
“Ferrari’s position is clear, has not changed, and Ferrari has made its choices already. We have confidence, full confidence, in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so,” she said.
“Everybody, they are still creating a lot of different stories around Fred and this is not useful. We do not intend to fuel speculation or comment on assumptions coming from outside the company.”

highlights.title: The Witcher 3 surges to its highest Steam concurrent player-count ever, following Remastered edition's release
highlights.summary: The Witcher 3 's newly released Remastered edition has dramatically rekindled interest in the 11-year-old role-playing game, which is currently enjoying its highest concurrent player-count on Steam ever.
body: As of the time of writing, nearly 120,000 people are playing The Witcher 3 on Steam, making it the ninth most-played game on the PC platform. That of course does not include numbers from the likes of GOG and the Epic Games Store, where it's also being sold, nor the players on PlayStation, Switch 2, and Xbox.

According to Steam data-tracking website SteamDB, that's the highest concurrent player-count The Witcher 3 has ever had - higher than at its launch in 2015 (a high of 92K), and higher than the game's previous peak of 103K in January 2020, when Netflix's Witcher show was at its most popular. The other notable peak was 89K in December 2022, when the next-gen update dropped.

With a playerbase of 65 million, there's a large community to excite, but it's a reminder of how much pulling-power CD Projekt Red's fantasy RPG has, all the same. And as America wakes up and downloads the update, the question is how high can the numbers go?

Sephora relaunched in the UK in 2023 with huge fanfare and now has about 18 stand-alone British stores. The company is owned by LVMH, the luxury goods group led by Bernard Arnault, who with his family is among the world’s richest people with a $171bn (£129bn) fortune, according to Forbes.

The company has rapidly expanded on its second attempt to enter the UK market after closing a handful of stores in 2005, having failed make a dent in a competitive sector. The deal with M&S marks a new strategy in its expansion plans.

Analysts have said Sephora’s work with up-and-coming brands and collaborations with high-profile influencers on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube has helped the company reach its target female audience of 24- to 36-year-olds.

highlights.title: Manchester City found guilty on all Premier League charges over rule breaches
highlights.summary: ‘Sham’ contracts helped inflate revenues by £900m. Commission finds club guilty over nine-season period. Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, the league has announced.
body: Manchester City breached Premier League financial rules by creating “sham” contracts to help inflate revenue and reduce costs by more than £900m over a nine-year period, an independent commission found.

The league announced on Tuesday that City had been found guilty on all charges related to serious breaches of its financial rules between seasons 2009-10 and 2017-18. It said a sanction would be addressed in a further hearing with the commission.

City created a number of commercial deals with sponsors that were part of a scheme to disguise where the funding was coming from, the commission concluded. Companies were required to pay only a portion of the stipulated fees, with the remainder funded by the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment + Development Ltd (Adug), which owned the club.
